summary: Ayinapalli Aiyappan was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Madras (~1923–1927). He served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1969–1970).

Ayu Khandro was a Tibetan Buddhist practitioner who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Drodul Pawo Dorje, Nyala Pema Dündul, and Chokgyur Lingpa. She later taught A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé and Namkhai Norbu.
Ayush Maheshwari works in computational fields and Indology. He completed his PhD and held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.

Ayya Khema studied under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Narada Mahathera, and Matara Sri Nyanarama. She founded Wat Buddha Dhamma, Jhana Verlag, and Sakyadhita, and served as a teacher at Buddha-Haus in 1989.
Azizah Nur is a doctoral student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

B. Alan Wallace is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at UCSD, Göttingen, Amherst, and Stanford (PhD under Carl Bielefeldt), alongside traditional teachers. He taught at Rabten Choeling, UCSB (~1997–2001), and founded the Santa Barbara Institute.

B. N. Goswamy was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University (~1950–1961). He served in the Indian Administrative Service (~1956–1958) and later held a post at Panjab University (~1958).

B. N. K. Sharma studied at the University of Madras and under Satyadhyana Tirtha. In Indology and philosophy, he held posts at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, Poornaprajna Sanskrit College, Dr. A. V. Baliga College, and Ramnarain Ruia College.

B. R. Ambedkar studied at Columbia University, the London School of Economics, and the University of Bonn. Active in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he taught at Sydenham College and was principal of Government Law College, Mumbai.

B. R. Gopal worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts with the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1964), the Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1965), and Epigraphia Carnatica (attested 1974).

B. R. Sharma is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Assistant Director of Research at Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005) and as a scientist at the Arid Forest Research Institute in 2020.

Baatr Kitinov earned his PhD in World History at Moscow State University. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history, he served as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Baburam Saksena was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1937–1938). He later served as Vice-Chancellor of Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University (~1964–1966).

Baden Henry Baden-Powell was an Indologist and historian who studied at St Paul's School and the University of Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1861–1889) and became Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab, which he founded.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra studied at University of the Punjab and Leiden University under Jean Philippe Vogel. He served as Government Epigraphist for India, held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, and was Professor at Panjab University (~1965–1969).
Baiei Henmi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and archaeology who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1915–1918) and later held a post at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1952), Peking University (~1952–1956), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and its Institute of Philosophy from ~1978 to 1995.

Baij Nath Puri was an Indian historian and archaeologist who completed his D.Phil. at Oxford (~1948–1951). He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1957–1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak studied at Elphinstone College, Deccan College, and Government Law College, Mumbai. An Indologist and historian, he co-founded the Deccan Education Society and taught mathematics at the New English School and Fergusson College.

Bal Krishen Thapar studied at University of the Punjab, Taxila, Heidelberg, and under Mortimer Wheeler. He was Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and co-founded the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage.
